messages:
maria: hi support, customer ran into a weird embeddings failure — they send a single item and we return a dimension mismatch. customer says: "expected 1536, got 1". they pasted the request and stack below. any quick checks? :thinking:

maria: request body they used (redacted):
```json
{
  "input": "This is a test sentence."
}
```

maria: response (truncated):
```
400 Bad Request
{"error":"embedding vector length mismatch: expected 1536, got 1"}
```

sam: thanks, can you confirm which client / SDK version and whether they're using the embeddings batch or single endpoint? also need headers (content-type, accept).

maria: client is a small python wrapper custom code (requests). headers they sent: no explicit content-type set, defaulting to text/plain. they passed the raw string as the body — looks like they didn't json-encode the payload.

jules: oof. that often yields the server trying to parse a string and treating each character or the entire string as a single scalar leading to weird shapes. can you repro locally? if so include curl.

maria: i repro'd quickly — when i POST plaintext body `This is a test` to /v1/embeddings it returns the same mismatch. when i send JSON with proper content-type it works.

jules: paste of failing curl:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  --data 'This is a test'
```

jules: working curl (note content-type and JSON array):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":["This is a test"]}'
```

eng-ml-oncall: confirmed — embeddings endpoint accepts either a single string or a list of strings in our API surface, but our backend JSON parser relies on Content-Type header to decide how to deserialize. if you send raw text it ends up as a single token stream that maps to a numeric scalar (hence dim=1).

eng-ml-oncall: more nuance: some client wrappers accidentally double-wrap arrays. e.g., this will also fail: `{"input": [["one","two"]]}` -> backend sees shape [1,1,N] instead of [N] or [1,N] and will try to compute a single embedding per top-level element producing unexpected dims.

maria: customer also reported intermittent latency spikes when batch size > 64. could this be related?

eng-ml-oncall: potentially — if the client is sending nested arrays the service may treat each nested container as a single long input, increasing tokenization cost and causing variable latencies. also malformed payloads often skip batching fast paths so throughput drops.

sam: action items?

jules: reply to customer with: 1) ensure Content-Type: application/json; 2) always send `input` as a JSON array for bulk requests (even if length 1) e.g. `{"input":["...","..."]}`; 3) confirm no extra nesting — arrays-of-arrays. include working curl.

jules: add a quick client-side validation snippet we can paste into support reply:
```python
# shallow validation
import json
if isinstance(body, str):
    raise ValueError("payload must be JSON; set Content-Type: application/json")
try:
    parsed = json.loads(body)
except Exception:
    raise ValueError("invalid JSON")
if 'input' not in parsed:
    raise ValueError("missing 'input' field")
if isinstance(parsed['input'], list):
    # ensure not nested
    if any(isinstance(i, list) for i in parsed['input']):
        raise ValueError("input must be a flat list of strings, not nested arrays")
```

support-bot: automated note — flagged as escalated to eng-ml; ticket #INC-2026 created and linked to the thread. :ticket:

maria: customer confirmed the JSON fix worked (they had been sending plaintext). they also removed an accidental nested wrapper added by an internal adapter. latency stable after fix. :tada:

sam: closing loop: recommend we add a client error message change: if Content-Type != application/json respond with 400 + guidance text rather than the generic dim mismatch. filing a small eng task.

eng-ml-oncall: i created a PR that improves error messaging and adds an extra server-side validation for nested arrays. will queue for next patch release. PR link: https://git.redwood/infra/embeddings/patch-req-129 (internal).

maria: thanks all — i'll send the customer the validated snippet and the follow-up notes.
